# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6 (Bu-Vb Np6)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Np6
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya

**Title (English, from literature):** Asking an unrelated person for a robe

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6, titled *Aññātakaviññatti* ("Asking an unrelated person for a robe"), sets forth the training rule regarding the solicitation of robe material from non-relatives [SuttaCentral]. Because monastics are expected to live on whatever requisites are freely offered rather than asking lay supporters for robes, soliciting cloth from an unrelated householder constitutes an offense requiring forfeiture and confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*), unless an exceptional circumstance applies—specifically, if the monk's robes have been stolen, lost, or destroyed [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1982]. Modern English translation of the rule and its accompanying narrative analysis is available by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
The rule is widely attested across early Buddhist monastic lineages. Curated parallels exist in the Pātimokkhas, Vibhaṅgas, and Parivāra of the Theravāda, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions, surviving in Pāli, Chinese, Sanskrit, Gāndhārī, and Tibetan recensions, with parallel regulations also preserved for the nuns' order (e.g., Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga NP 16 in Pāli and NP 4 or 6 in other schools) [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1982]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates these correspondences, aligning the text cross-linguistically with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra*, as well as demonstrating substantial internal Pāli reuse with adjacent robe-solicitation rules (notably Bu-Vb Np4, Np5, Np8, Np9, Np10, and Np27) and Khandhaka passages in Kd 1 and Kd 6 [DharmaNexus].
